extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media critics, and readers interested in political-media accountability
extracted.subtask_description: A blog-style collection of commentary and criticism aimed at diagnosing problems in contemporary political journalism and proposing how coverage should change to better inform the electorate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Watch mission statement: Political journalism needs a reset
rubrics_metrics.description: No one can possibly argue that modern political journalism has fulfilled its essential mission of creating an informed electorate. Here's how it needs to change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the umbrella claim motivating the site: evaluate journalism by whether it helps create an informed electorate and consider reforms when it fails to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trump’s Second Term
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage and critique focused on how journalists report on a hypothetical or actual second term of Donald Trump.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a topical lens for assessing whether reporting adequately addresses risks, accountability, and the president's fitness for office; no further guidance on specific scoring provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: New York Times
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation and commentary directed at The New York Times' political coverage and editorial choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the Times as a subject for critique—assess reporting quality, framing, omissions, and whether presentation meets the needs of readers; the page lists related articles critiquing the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Washington Post
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation and commentary directed at The Washington Post's political coverage and editorial choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to the Times entry: use as a category for assessing whether the Post's reporting and presentation serve the public interest; page links to critiques and calls for stronger stances.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Biden Presidency
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage and critique concerning how journalists report on the Biden administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a topical area to judge balance, scrutiny, and thoroughness in coverage of the incumbent administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campaign Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how journalists cover political campaigns, including framing, emphasis on horse-race elements, and voter information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied criterion: evaluate whether campaign reporting informs voters vs. indulges in superficial competition-focused coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy in Danger
rubrics_metrics.description: A topical category concerning reporting that relates to threats to democratic institutions or norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this lens to judge whether press coverage adequately recognizes and conveys risks to democratic processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewrite Desk
rubrics_metrics.description: A category (likely focused on how press narratives are rewritten or summarized) used to critique press framing and narrative choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether rewriting/summary practices distort, dilute, or clarify complex issues for readers; page does not provide explicit scoring rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: A thematic focus on the concept of journalistic objectivity and how it is applied or misapplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as an evaluative axis: does invocation of 'objectivity' hide moral judgments, create false balance, or serve readers' understanding? The page is critical of conventional uses of objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: False Equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: A topic/category calling out instances where journalists present unequal positions as equally valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reporting for inappropriate balance that obscures truth or significance; the site highlights false equivalence as a recurring problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covering Race
rubrics_metrics.description: A topical category about how the press covers race-related matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether reporting on race is thorough, contextually informed, and attentive to harm and power dynamics; no detailed checklist is provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: A theme concerning the use (and potential overuse) of anonymous sources in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether reliance on anonymity is warranted and whether it diminishes accountability or clarity for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trump and the Coronavirus
rubrics_metrics.description: A topical category focused on reporting at the intersection of coverage of Trump and the COVID-19 pandemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether journalists properly connected leadership actions and public-health consequences; the site uses this as an example of coverage failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horse-Race Journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: A topic criticizing journalism that emphasizes competition and polling over substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as an evaluative criterion: does coverage prioritize sensational or competitive elements over policy, context, and voter information?

rubrics_metrics.name: Fighting Disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: A category focusing on the press's role in combating falsehoods and misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether outlets actively identify and correct disinformation, and whether they explain why claims are false rather than merely reporting disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: A topical strand dealing with the role of advocacy in journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether and when advocacy is appropriate, transparent, or necessary given the stakes; the site appears to support stronger stances in certain contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add clear disclaimers/context when covering Trump
rubrics_metrics.description: With a few words that simply state the obvious, news outlets could help their readers understand why all this is happening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance implied by a post title and excerpt: journalists should add short disclaimers or context to help readers interpret behavior and claims, particularly regarding figures like Trump; the page suggests this is an easy, high-impact change.
